questions.question: What does the narrator say about Rome's origins that makes its rise surprising?

options.text: Rome was originally a powerful military kingdom.
It was a very small Greek city state that rose to such great heights.
Rome was founded by barbarian tribes from the north.
Rome started as a wealthy trading republic.

questions.correctAnswer: It was a very small Greek city state that rose to such great heights.

questions.question: According to the documentary, what officially drove Rome's expansionism?

options.text: The desire to spread Roman culture and language.
The ambition of individual emperors for personal glory.
Defensive considerations — protecting itself and its allies.
The need to find new agricultural land for its population.

questions.correctAnswer: Defensive considerations — protecting itself and its allies.

questions.question: In the context of the clip, what does the word 'undergirded' most closely mean?

options.text: Undermined and weakened over time.
Funded with public money.
Provided the essential foundation and support for.
Was considered separate and unrelated to.

questions.correctAnswer: Provided the essential foundation and support for.

questions.question: Why does the narrator compare Rome at its peak to a roller coaster at the top of a hill?

options.text: To show how exciting it was to be a Roman citizen.
To illustrate that Romans deliberately chose to slow their expansion.
To suggest Rome felt triumphant while unaware decline was about to begin.
To explain how Rome's military strategy changed in the 2nd century.

questions.correctAnswer: To suggest Rome felt triumphant while unaware decline was about to begin.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this documentary clip?

options.text: Rome's success was entirely due to its military discipline and technology.
The rise of Rome was inevitable given its geography and resources.
Rome's extraordinary rise contained the very seeds of its eventual collapse.
Barbarian tribes were the sole cause of the fall of the Roman Empire.

questions.correctAnswer: Rome's extraordinary rise contained the very seeds of its eventual collapse.

questions.question: What tone do the historians use when describing Rome's situation in the 3rd century crisis?

options.text: Celebratory — admiring Rome's resilience under pressure.
Neutral and purely statistical — listing facts without comment.
Ominous and analytical — conveying inevitability and slow collapse.
Humorous — using irony to mock Rome's overconfidence.

questions.correctAnswer: Ominous and analytical — conveying inevitability and slow collapse.

slides.title: Language focus: Modals of possibility
slides.content:
Modals of possibility is a structure that shows up right in the dialogue you just watched. Two things matter: the form, and when you'd actually use it.
• Use MODAL + base verb to talk about what is possible, likely or hypothetical.
• Would / could / might soften the claim — they signal an opinion, not a fact.
• The base verb after the modal never takes -s or -ed: "she might come", not "she might comes".
The lines below are your anchor — every time you drill Modals of possibility in the next slide, come back to them.
